sections.title: $C^{0}$ stability of torsion-free $G_{2}$ structures along the Laplacian flow
sections.abstract: The authors claim that torsion-free $G_{2}$-structures are dynamically stable under Laplacian flow for closed initial structures in a $C^{0}$ neighbourhood.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove that, on a compact 7-manifold, closed $G_{2}$-structures sufficiently close in $C^{0}$ to a torsion-free structure flow for all time and converge smoothly to its identity-component diffeomorphism orbit.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A compact 7-manifold, a torsion-free reference $G_{2}$-structure, and a closed initial $G_{2}$-structure in the same cohomology class and sufficiently close in $C^{0}$.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem has the compact-manifold and fixed-cohomology-class hypotheses above; this report has not independently checked the proof.

sections.title: Ordering Is Not Deciding: Towards Preference-Consistent Multi-Objective Design–Decision Optimisation
sections.abstract: The authors construct multi-objective examples showing that Pareto filtering can discard the solution with the highest aggregated actor preference, while their IMAP method retains it.
sections.claimed_result: Across constructed design-decision problems, the authors show that Pareto optimality does not guarantee preference-consistent choice; IMAP can identify a best-fit solution that Pareto filtering removes.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Constructed problems with two system performances, up to four preference functions from up to two actors, and both independent/interdependent and monotone/non-monotone preference relationships.
sections.unique_caveat: The comparison is demonstrated on deliberately simplified constructed cases; it does not establish comparative performance on real-world decision problems.

sections.title: Uniform Positivity of the $F$-Signature and Pure Descent of klt Singularities
sections.abstract: The authors characterize klt-type singularities through uniform positive lower bounds for the $F$-signatures of their reductions modulo sufficiently large primes, and apply this to pure descent.
sections.claimed_result: For a normal complex singularity, the authors prove that klt type yields a uniform positive lower bound for $F$-signatures on an open set of large-characteristic reductions, while non-klt type forces those signatures below every positive threshold on an open set; they also give a reduction-mod-$p$ proof of pure descent.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Normal complex varieties spread out over a finite-type model over $\mathbb{Z}$; conclusions concern closed points in nonempty open subsets of the model and hence sufficiently large-prime reductions.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors explicitly do not resolve the separate conjecture that klt type is equivalent to strong $F$-regularity of reductions for all sufficiently large primes; their characterization is via uniform $F$-signature bounds.

sections.title: Optimal Scheduling of Multi-Site AI Data Centers in Day-Ahead Markets
sections.abstract: The authors formulate multi-site AI data-center scheduling as a linear program and report 6.3% lower energy costs at equal work in a year-long simulation on 2025 CAISO prices.
sections.claimed_result: In their 2025 California ISO day-ahead-price simulation across three data-center markets, coordinated scheduling lowers fleet energy cost by 6.3% at equal work.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A modeled fleet with GPU power caps, deferrable jobs and deadlines, inference response-time slack, site power, and day-ahead electricity prices; results come from a year-long simulation.
sections.unique_caveat: The 6.3% saving is specific to the stated simulation, market data, and modeled operating modes; it is not evidence from a deployed fleet.

sections.title: Nondegeneracy and uniqueness of ground states of the Schrödinger equation with Neumann conditions in a weakly nonlocal regime
sections.abstract: For a fractional Schrödinger equation with nonlocal Neumann conditions in a half-space and order $2s$ with $s$ near 1, the authors prove ground-state nondegeneracy and uniqueness up to tangential translations and sign.
sections.claimed_result: In the stated weakly nonlocal half-space setting, the kernel of the linearized equation consists only of tangential derivatives of the ground state, implying uniqueness modulo tangential translations and sign.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A fractional Laplacian of order $2s$ with $s$ close to 1, posed in a half-space with nonlocal Neumann conditions.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract restricts the result to the weakly nonlocal regime ($s$ close to 1) and half-space Neumann setting; it does not claim the same theorem for other boundary conditions or parameter regimes.

sections.title: Noncommutative Geometry, Spectral Asymptotics, and Semiclassical Analysis, II. Operator-Theoretic Tools
sections.abstract: The paper proves operator-theoretic tools for spectral triples, including a fractional-commutator factorization and a Tauberian result deriving Weyl laws from suitable zeta-function or heat-trace conditions.
sections.claimed_result: The author establishes three results: a factorization for fractional commutators via double operator integrals, extensions of a lemma for arbitrary unital spectral triples, and a Tauberian theorem yielding Weyl laws for operators $aD^2a$ under the stated zeta/heat-trace conditions.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Operator theory for spectral triples and positive invertible algebra elements; the Tauberian conclusion applies when the specified zeta-function or heat-trace conditions hold.
sections.unique_caveat: The Weyl-law conclusion is conditional on those analytic hypotheses; the abstract does not claim unconditional asymptotics for arbitrary operators or triples.

sections.title: Comodule algebras and the cohomology of symplectic groups
sections.abstract: The authors make symplectic-group homology with Steinberg-module coefficients into a comodule algebra over the corresponding general-linear-group homology and derive lower bounds for cohomology of arithmetic symplectic groups.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove a comodule-algebra structure and a freeness-type result, then deduce new lower bounds for high-dimensional cohomology of symplectic groups over number rings and their congruence subgroups.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Group homology with Steinberg module coefficients for symplectic and general linear groups, with applications to symplectic groups over number rings and congruence subgroups.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not specify the numerical form or range of the resulting cohomological lower bounds; those details require the full theorem statements.

sections.title: Antipodal Parity and Second-Chaos Regge Curvature on Random Hyperplane Arrangements
sections.abstract: For orientation-reversal-invariant random hyperplanes, the paper proves parity cancellations for signed Regge curvature and a second-chaos limit for isotropic Gaussian normals on bounded windows.
sections.claimed_result: Under orientation-reversal invariance, the signed curvature has zero mean and zero first Hoeffding component; in the isotropic Gaussian bounded-window setting it converges after rescaling to a second-chaos series, with a planar cone-angle limit law under finite fourth moments.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Independent oriented hyperplanes in Euclidean space; orientation-reversal invariance for the parity result, isotropic Gaussian normals on bounded windows for the second-chaos limit, and finite fourth moments for the planar global limit law.
sections.unique_caveat: The limit theorems use distinct distributional hypotheses; the abstract does not claim a common universal limit for arbitrary hyperplane laws in every dimension.

sections.title: On the non-extendibility of triangular $D(n)$-pairs $\{n,2n\}$ with $n = 2k^2 \pm k
sections.abstract: For a specified finite set of odd $k$ and signs satisfying a prime condition, the authors prove that triangular $D(n)$-pairs $\{n,2n\}$ cannot be extended to quadruples and formulate a broader conjecture.
sections.claimed_result: For an explicitly determined finite set of $(k,\varepsilon)$ with odd positive $k$, $\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}$ and $4k+\varepsilon$ prime, the pair with $n=2k^2+\varepsilon k$ is not extendible to a triangular $D(n)$-quadruple.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Positive-integer triangular $D(n)$-tuples; the result is for the special pair $\{n,2n\}$ and a finite explicitly determined parameter set satisfying the stated parity and primality conditions.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem covers only the listed finite parameter set; the broader non-extendibility phenomenon is stated as a conjecture, not established generally.

sections.title: Arithmetic Upper and Lower Bounds for the Denumerant Function II
sections.abstract: The author sharpens prior upper and lower bounds for Sylvester's denumerant function for arbitrary positive integer inputs, including a binomial-sum lower bound along multiples of their gcd.
sections.claimed_result: Applying an arithmetic argument from the preceding paper in the series, the author obtains a larger binomial-sum lower bound that needs no representability assumption on multiples of the gcd and reduces the shift in Agnarsson's upper bound.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Sylvester's denumerant function for arbitrary positive integers $a_1,\dots,a_k$; the lower bound applies along multiples of $\gcd(a_1,\dots,a_k)$.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper supplies improved bounds rather than an exact formula for arbitrary inputs and is the second paper in a series.
